columns.Description: Processors determine what option to use for values placed in the Destination Identifier field in report records. When the acquiring or issuing identifier identification option is selected, the report Destination Identifier is placed in the Destination Identifier field of the machine-readable (TC 46) and print-ready (TC 47) report records. The acquiring or issuing identifier identification option should be selected if the processor wants report records in acquiring or issuing identifier sequence. If this option is not used, the Report Destination processor is placed in the Destination Identifier field. The processor is always in the report records for summary-level SREs.
Daily reports are delivered first. On the first processing day of each month, monthly reports for the previous month are delivered after the daily reports.

The VSS processor reports are delivered before the International Settlement Service and National Net Settlement Service reports. The daily VSS processor reports are delivered in this order: VSS-900–P VSS-900–PS Clients participating in a National Net Settlement Service receive two sets of reports: one for the National Net Settlement Service and one for the International Settlement service. If the National Net Settlement Service has a customized cutoff time, the reports for this service are delivered separately from the International Settlement Service reports. If the National Net Settlement Service has the same cutoff time as the Interna­ tional Settlement Service, reports for the National Net Settlement Service follow those for the International Settlement Service in the same delivery. columns.Contents: VSS report IDs have three parts separated by dashes. The first part always contains the literal “VSS.” The second part is the alphanumeric report identifier. The third part indicates the type of report: Processor report (P) Processor summary report (PS) Client summary report (S) Client monthly report (M) Client weekly report (W) Client revised report (R) The absence of the third part of the report ID indicates that the report is a client daily report.

Appendix B VSS Reports-Machine-Readable Formats Machine-readable (TC 46) records are organized by VisaNet Settlement Service (VSS) report. Each report line of data has one or two records, depending on the transaction format used. Common report information appears in the first record for each report line of data. If a second record is required, the common report information is not included in that record. The transaction format used for the machine-readable record depends on the report. Each record begins with a “46” (positions 1 and 2), and all reports belong to Report Group V (position 59). There are nine (9) different transaction formats, identified by the Report Subgroup (position 60). All transaction formats consist of one transaction component record (TCR), except for Report Subgroups 4, 6, and 9, which consist of two TCRs. The TCR is identified in Transaction Component Sequence Number (position 4). Single Message System (SMS)-connected clients using a Direct Access Service (DAS) VisaNet Access Point (VAP) for report delivery receive the machine-readable records in the file type of SETLM. SMS-connected clients using non-VAP delivery receive the machine-readable records as a separate transmission. There is no header or trailer record. BASE II-connected clients and SMS-connected clients using a BASE II VAP receive the machine- readable records in their Center Transaction File (CTF)—Incoming Interchange.

blocks.text: Single Message System (SMS) reports and raw data are available for clients connected to SMS.
SMS-connected clients may elect to receive SMS reports that detail a client's transaction activity. Subscription is optional for all SMS reports.
SMS-connected clients can also choose to receive raw data records that detail client transaction activity for the processing day. Raw data
allows the clients to analyze and customize their Single Message System data in the way that best suits their business needs.
See V.I.P. System VisaNet Authorization-Only Online Messages Technical Specifications and SMS Technical Specifications.
SMS reports are identified by a combination of report number and sort criteria.
The second position of the report number indicates the report category.
The third position of the report number indicates whether the report is intended for an issuer, an acquirer, or both.
Issuer reports have an even number.
Acquirer reports have an odd number.
Reports that apply to both issuers and acquirers have an even number.
The final position of the report identifier indicates the sort criteria.
The SMS reports are listed in this table.
Clients can subscribe to multiple sorts of the same report number.

blocks.text: SMS reports have four levels of reporting entities.
The four levels of reporting entities are:
The funds transfer SRE is the level at which funds transfer occurs. The funds transfer SRE can be at any level in the VSS hierarchy.
A processor is a Visa endpoint (or Visa-approved third-party) that provides authorization, clearing, or settlement services for merchants and
clients. The processor captures transactions counts and amounts online. A running total of counts and amounts is accumulated every 30
minutes. The system stores these totals as advice messages (0520) for recovery by the processor.
The affiliate ID can be an issuer, an acquirer, or both. Transactions for all card ranges assigned to an affiliate ID appear on the affiliate IDs
SMS reports generate a total and force a page-break any time a reporting level changes. So, if a client has an affiliate ID associated
with multiple SREs or processors, it may be necessary to add the subtotals to obtain the total activity for an affiliate.
For SMS reports at the affiliate level, the 10-digit number in the header has:
The 6-digit identifier of the issuer or acquirer.
The 4-digit Network ID (0002 for Visa, 0003 for Interlink, 0004 for Plus).
The lowest-level SRE is the lowest level at which VSS produces settlement reports. The combination of the funds transfer SRE, processor, and
affiliate ID identifies the lowest-level SRE displayed on the SMS report.
The SMS transaction detail reports (SMS600–SMS617) cumulatively reflect all of a client's interchange transactions for one processing day.
The reports assist the client center to reconcile its position with the V.I.P. System by providing a detailed transaction listing for the issuer or
acquirer at the affiliate ID level. Subtotals are provided for each affiliate ID. Reports also generate a subtotal and force a page-break any
time a client reporting level changes. For example, if one affiliate ID has activity with two processors, the report will have two affiliate
Reports are produced daily for delivery to the subscriber. Subscription is optional for all transaction detail reports.
The SMS exception detail reports (SMS610–SMS617) are a subset of the transaction detail reports. Exception detail reports display a
particular category of the client's exception transactions for one processing day.
These transactions are also displayed on the SMS600 or SMS601 report. Exception detail reports have the same functionality and fields as
